description: A free Chromium browser for the Mac: Arc's sidebar, Dia's polish. Chat on Discord: discord.gg/TdhuXrbcA6

latest_release.name: Ardia 0.2.44
latest_release.body:
## New

- **Sidebar on the right**: pick Right under the layout cards in Make it yours, in Settings › Tabs › Sidebar position, or with View › Sidebar on Right. The window buttons move with it, and the hidden sidebar peeks in from the right and stays open while you look at it.
- **Share a pinned folder through iCloud Drive**: right-click it and choose Share Folder… to keep it in `iCloud Drive › Ardia Shared` and share it with macOS's own share sheet. No account needed. Links sync both ways, per profile, and open from Finder too.
- **Profiles that share browsing data can share their Top Apps**, as Arc's spaces share Favorites. Pin, rename, reorder or folder a tile in one and it changes in all, and each tile stays one live page across profiles. Each profile has its own switch in Settings › Profiles › Shared data, in its details and in its right-click menu. Thanks, [@ymehili](https://github.com/mantrakp04/ardia/pull/136).
- **Set Ardia up from files**, dotfiles style: settings, keybindings and themes can live in `~/.config/ardia/config.json` and `themes/<name>.json`. Ardia applies them at launch and on every save, and never writes them back. The same file can add your own address bar rows, from a list, a URL template or a suggest endpoint.
- **Hooks**: rules in `~/.config/ardia/hooks.json` can rewrite or block links before they open, send links from a given app to a profile, file finished downloads into a folder, deny camera or microphone requests, or run a command when something happens. Anything that reaches outside the page you're on waits until you approve it in Settings › Advanced › Automation.
- **The `ardia` command can drive Ardia**: with "Let the ardia command control Ardia" on, it runs commands, lists windows, and `ardia browse` takes agent-browser's commands and runs them on the Ardia you have open.
- **A real emoji picker** for profile and sidebar icons: search, every emoji by category, and SF Symbols, with the current icon highlighted.
- **Share from the page menu**: right-click to share selected text, an image, a link (trackers removed) or the page. File › Share › Share… is now ⌥⌘S.
- **Custom themes from the New Tab page**: "Make it yours" now has the Custom swatch and the gradient editor from Settings.
- **The sidebar player shows the time left** where its pause button was, ticking while it plays. Pause is one hover away.
- **New-tab links can stay in Little Ardia**: turn on Settings › General › "Open new-tab links inside Little Ardia" and a link that would open a new tab loads in Little Ardia itself, so Back takes you back. Thanks, [@narasaka](https://github.com/mantrakp04/ardia/pull/344).
- **A pull request folder can hide repos.** Its menu has a Repositories submenu, as Arc's does. Thanks, [@maciekzygmunt](https://github.com/mantrakp04/ardia/pull/309).
- **Picture in Picture's corners line up with the window's**: thrown into a corner, its curve nests inside the browser window's rounded corner.

## Faster

| | 0.2.43 | 0.2.44 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| New tab, first paint | 80 ms | 69 ms | 14% faster |
| New tab, its page's first frame | 55 ms | 45 ms | 18% faster |
| New window, first paint | 106 ms | 98 ms | 8% faster |

A new tab now shows its page about 10 ms sooner.

## Fixed

- **Pages scroll smoothly with the sidebar open in the Glass style.** Every Top Apps tile cost its own pass each frame, and scrolling stuttered. The tiles now render in one.
- **Typing some words with dashes and dots no longer freezes the address bar.** Text like `my-post.another-post.x:` stalled each keystroke for seconds and could crash Ardia.
- **Three more crashes are gone**: the green button's Move & Resize and Fill & Arrange menus on macOS 27, any page that started a service worker while an `ardia` session was connected, and running low on disk space.
- **Picture in Picture works in WebKit tabs**, including for a video embedded in another site's player, and its Back to Tab takes you to the video when you were in a split view

Touch grass.

Arc’s sidebar and Dia’s polish on real Chromium.
Free and open source. Ads and trackers stay out.

Download Ardia 0.2.44 for Mac

121 MB DMG · macOS 14 Sonoma or later · Apple Silicon · Notarized by Apple

## Lose the toolbar. Move the address bar into the sidebar and the page runs all the way to the top of the window. ## Two pages, one window. Drag a tab onto the page. Up to three panes, side by side or stacked. ## Refuses to leave the picture. Switch tabs mid-video and it floats along in the corner. Go back to its tab and it slips back into the page. ## Your extensions come along. The Chrome Web Store just works, its button says Add to Ardia, and Sync takes them to your other Macs. ## Ads and trackers stay out. The full uBlock Origin is built in, cookie banners included. Google’s pings are compiled out. Crash reports are opt-in and never carry your sites or searches. ## Also in there - **Work stays at work.** Each profile keeps its own logins, history, extensions and colour. Swipe the sidebar to switch. - **Little Ardia.** ⌥⌘N opens a small window with one page and no sidebar. - **Groups on contact.** Drop a tab on a tab and they’re a group, named for you. - **Moves in for you.** Bookmarks, history, passwords and logins from Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Arc, Dia and five more. Arc’s spaces, pinned tabs and themes too. - **Paints like Arc.** Gradient themes per profile: up to three colours, some grain, some blur. - **Syncs through your iCloud.** End-to-end encrypted, in a folder in your own iCloud Drive. No server of ours in the middle. - **Command bar.** ⌘L finds tabs, history and bookmarks, does your sums, and knows doc.new and 16 friends. - **Tidies up.** ⌥⌘K sweeps the tabs you haven’t touched into Recently Cleaned. - **Clean links.** Copy a link and the tracking junk stays behind. - **Naps when you do.** Background tabs past your latest five freeze, and sleep after half an hour. - **Sits still.** Idles under half a percent of CPU with a tab open. - **Updates itself.** Quietly, then shows you what changed. ## It’s actually Chromium. Not WebKit. Not Electron. Every window is Chrome’s own, so sites, extensions and DevTools behave like they do in Chrome. | Part | Details | Status | | --- | --- | --- | | Engine | Chromium 156, on Chrome’s own framework. | ✓ Yes | | De-Googled | Google’s background services stripped out. | ✓ Yes | | H.264 and AAC | The codecs Chromium leaves out. | ✓ Yes | | DevTools | Docked, with device mode. Like Chrome. | ✓ Yes | | Sync | End-to-end encrypted, through your own iCloud Drive. | ✓ Yes | | Translate | On your Mac. Nothing leaves it. | ✓ macOS 26 | | Passkeys | Touch ID yes. iCloud Keychain waits on Apple. | ~ Partly | | Netflix and DRM | Streaming sites open in WebKit, where they play. Widevine in Chromium waits on Google. | ~ Partly | | Intel Macs | Apple Silicon only. | ✗ No |

Download Ardia 0.2.44

It’s 121 MB and one drag into Applications.
Not on a Mac? Watch › Custom › Releases up top and GitHub tells you when it is.

--- # Build it yourself A macOS browser that looks and feels like [Dia](https://diabrowser.com): Chrome's own framework from our patched Chromium with our layer on top (ArdiaCore), an Expo + React Native macOS shell, and Metal shaders reconstructed from Dia's own New Tab effects. ``` apps/ browser/ Expo + react-native-macos app (UI in src/, Xcode project in macos/) packages/ ardiacore/ The engine: Chromium 156's framework with our layer (Chrome tabs hosted in our views), JS API in src/ shell/ Native menu bar + shortcuts → JS, windows, SF Symbols, native primitives shaders/ Metal: New Tab effects + grained OKLab window backdrop import/ Import from other browsers (bookmarks, history, passwords, Arc spaces) core/ Pure TS: omnibox input → URL, suggestions, Dia-style breadcrumbs (tested) ``` ## Run it Requires Xcode 26+, CocoaPods, Node 22.13+ (pinned in `.nvmrc`), pnpm 11. ```bash pnpm install ``` The engine (Chrome's framework, built from our patched Chromium) comes prebuilt: with no local engine build, the app's build downloads the one matching your checkout's `engine/` (about 110 MB, once; Apple Silicon only) and checks it against `packages/ardiacore/prebuilt-engines.tsv`. Every release whose engine changed publishes one. If `main`'s engine is newer than the last release's, work from a release tag (`v0.2.30`, say), or run `packages/ardiacore/scripts/fetch-engine.sh --nearest` to build against the newest prebuilt anyway. Passkeys and saved cards need our team ID and won't work in a build signed by anyone else. To change the engine itself (anything under `engine/`), build it from source: Chrome's framework from our patched Chromium tree in `~/chromium-build` (Chromium 156.0.8078.79 with the patch series in `engine/patches`; `docs/engine-build.md` › "Rebuilding", then `engine/chromium/apply.sh`, `engine/ardiacore/apply.sh` and `autoninja -C out/Release_GN_arm64 chrome_framework`; the first build takes about 2 hours). The app's build stages it from there when it exists. ```bash pnpm pods ``` In one terminal, start Metro: ```bash pnpm dev ``` In another, build and launch the Debug app (on its own data, `~/Library/Application Support/Ardia Dev`, or `ARDIA_DATA_DIR`): ```bash pnpm macos ``` Other tasks: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm shaders:check` (compiles the embedded Metal offline), `pnpm build` (Release `.app` with a Hermes bytecode bundle in `apps/browser/build/`). Signed releases (DMG, Sparkle zip and appcast): `scripts/release.sh `, see `docs/releasing.md`. Shortcuts: ⌘T new tab, ⌘L command bar, ⌘W close, ⇧⌘T reopen, ⌘S sidebar, ⌘[ / ⌘] back/forward, ⌘R reload, ⌘1–⌘9 select tab, ⌃Tab cycle. ## How Dia's New Tab light works Dia 1.50 turns this light off along with its rebrand (a painted mark, a single-colour power-up band and a halo around the bar; `docs/dia-spec.md` › "1.50 Sunglow"), and so does Ardia. The reconstruction left the tree with it: `git show f2c0e251:packages/shaders/ios/AreaLightView.swift`. These findings come from disassembling the Metal libraries in `Dia.app` (v1.49.1) with `xcrun metal-objdump`. `BoostBrowser_PowerUp.bundle/default.metallib` contains `breathingAreaLightFragment`, which the Swift class `NewTabPage.NewTabAreaLightView` hosts. The reconstruction was `AreaLightView.swift` (above). - **The command bar is a light source.** Dia models the bar as a rounded-rectangle area light floating `lift` points above the page. Each pixel receives the closed-form irradiance of that rectangle: the solid-angle formula, one `atan` term per corner, times 1/2π. Rounded corners subtract (1 − π/4) of each corner square. The result is a physically correct penumbra: a higher lift gives a softer, wider glow. - **Falloff** is reshaped from inverse-square to `(h/d)^falloff`, where `d` is the distance to the emitter's rounded-rect surface rather than to its centre. - **Colour** is Dia's brand spectrum (`ProgressBarColor2…7` in its asset catalog): blue `#0358F7`, steel `#5092C7`, lavender `#E1E1FE`, yellow `#FFD400`, orange `#FA3D1D` and magenta `#FD02F5`. It is laid out as a wrapping, slightly diagonal gradient that scrolls every 20 s. IQ's 2D simplex noise warps the gradient under the bar, and the warp fades out into the penumbra. - **Dark mode** treats the light as HDR emission and applies the Hable/Uncharted-2 filmic tonemap (white point 11.2), with alpha set to Rec.709 luminance. **Light mode** keeps the flat palette colour and uses the irradiance as opacity. - **Finishing:** alpha fades over the top 50 pt and bottom 200 pt of the view, and ±3/255 triangular dither (Dave Hoskins' `hash12`) prevents banding in the long soft falloff. - **Animation:** the shader itself only scrolls the colours. The lift-off intro and the slow "breathing" come from the CPU, which animates `lift` and `intensity`. Those curves live in Dia's Swift code, so the ones here (quartic ease-out over 1.1 s, ±7% intensity on a 5.5 s sine) are my approximation. The **window backdrop** comes from `ARC_WindowThemeUI.bundle` (`gradientFragment` + `renderFragment`). Gradient stops are stored and mixed in **OKLab**, then converted to linear sRGB and gamma-encoded in the shader. A tiled grain texture is then multiply-blended on top. `WindowBackdropView` does the same with procedural grain. Only math and colour values are reused. No Dia images, fonts or binaries are copied into this repo. ## Architecture notes - **Why Expo SDK 54:** `react-native-macos` tops out at 0.81, which pairs with Expo SDK 54 (whose `ExpoAppDelegate` / `ExpoReactNativeFactory` have macOS code paths). - **Legacy architecture.** react-native-macos 0.81's Fabric support is experimental, so the app runs on the legacy architecture. One consequence: Expo's legacy view-manager adapter instantiates a module's *first* view class for every view it declares, so each native view has its own module. - **Metro, not `expo start`.** Metro runs through the react-native-macos CLI. `metro.config.js` redirects `react-native` → `react-native-macos` for `platform=macos`, because defining our own `resolveRequest` replaces the redirect the CLI would install. - **No Reanimated.** It has no macOS build for 0.81; animations use RN's `Animated`. - **Monorepo paths.** pnpm is set to `nodeLinker: hoisted` because CocoaPods and Metro resolve `react-native-macos` by path. The Podfile rewrites `REACT_NATIVE_PATH` to the hoisted location and raises every pod's deployment target to 14.0, since Xcode 26+ rejects the 11.0 some Expo pods declare. - **Native subviews** are sized in `setFrameSize`, not `layout()`. RN macOS assigns frames directly and never autoresizes subviews. - **Shaders** are Metal source embedded in Swift and compiled at runtime (once per class, cached). This keeps the pods free of a metallib build phase. ## Status Feature parity with Dia (everything but its AI) is tracked row by row in [docs/dia-feature-parity.md](docs/dia-feature-parity.md); releases and their notes are at [ardia.dev/release-notes](https://ardia.dev/release-notes). ## License Ardia as distributed is licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3](LICENSE), because its engine is built with GPL-3.0 patches. Ardia's own source files are under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE.Apache-2.0). It builds on Chromium, carries a few of the Chromium Embedded Framework's patches to Chromium (BSD-3-Clause), and bundles uBlock Origin, each under its own license; see [NOTICE](NOTICE). Every release links its source.
